problem.text: The faces of each of $7$ standard dice are labeled with the integers from $1$ to $6$. Let $p$ be the probability that when all $7$ dice are rolled, the sum of the numbers on the top faces is $10$. What other sum occurs with the same probability $p$?

steps.title: Where to start: look for a symmetry
steps.body: We do not need to compute $p$. The question asks which other sum is exactly as likely, which hints at a symmetry that pairs low sums with high sums. A natural pairing on one die is $x \leftrightarrow 7 - x$, since $1 \leftrightarrow 6$, $2 \leftrightarrow 5$, $3 \leftrightarrow 4$.

your_turn.prompt: If a die shows $2$, what does the pairing turn it into?

steps.title: Flip every die
steps.body: Replace the number $x$ on every one of the $7$ dice by $7 - x$. Doing this twice gets you back where you started, so it pairs up all the outcomes one-to-one. That means a sum and the sum it turns into happen in the same number of ways, so they are equally likely.

your_turn.prompt: The roll $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 6$ has sum $27$. What are the flipped numbers and their sum?

steps.title: Find the matching sum
steps.body: Now find the partner of a sum without listing rolls. Each die changes from $x$ to $7 - x$, so a die's number and its flipped number always add to $7$. Careful: the partner of a sum is not found by subtracting it from the largest sum, $42$. That rule would send the largest sum, $42$, to $0$, which is not even a possible sum. The largest sum must be paired with the smallest, $7$.

your_turn.prompt: Which sum is paired with the smallest possible sum, $7$?
your_turn.answer: $42$: all ones flip to all sixes. Each of these sums happens in exactly one way.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
Paired sums always add to $7 \cdot 7 = 49$ (check: $27 + 22 = 49$ and $7 + 42 = 49$). So sum $10$ is paired with
$$49 - 10 = 39,$$
and these two sums have the same probability $p$. The answer is **(D)** $39$.

wrong_choices.C: $32$ comes from reflecting through the maximum, $42 - 10$. The flip sends a sum $S$ to $49 - S$ (for example, $7$ goes to $42$), so the partner of $10$ is $39$.

verification.verifier_notes: Hole found by adversarial verifier, fixed, and re-verified by a fresh verifier.
